newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rubber edges up on Tokyo, demand flat.
newsitem.headline: Thai rubber edges up on Tokyo, demand flat.

text.p: Thai rubber prices edged up slightly in a thin market on Tokyo gains and high local prices, traders said on Friday.
China and Japan entered the market and bought in moderate amounts as rubber in other markets were more attractively priced, they said.
"There is nothing to report really. Unless the prices dip from current levels, I don't expect to see active buying interest near-term," said one Bangkok-based trader.
"Buyers are likely to go elsewhere," he added.
Japan buyers bid at 115.00 U.S. cents a kg for the past two days but no sellers emerged at that level, they said.
Thai benchmark RSS3 was quoted around 116.00 US cents a kg for July shipment and at 116.50 US cents for August shipment, slighly firmer from Wednesday.

Government sources said the rubber intervention scheme, under which authorities buy unsmoked sheet grade 3 from local producers at 29.00 baht a kg continued, but declined to reveal the amount bought so far.
